info.description:
### 1. Global Invoice API Overview
Complete API for managing Electronic Invoices and Digital Receipts in full compliance with international tax regulations. This is a **Global Service** designed to handle multiple countries; while it currently focuses on the Italian market, it is built to integrate foreign invoicing services and cross-border digital tax compliance.

--- 

### 2. Italian Electronic Invoicing (Fatturazione Elettronica)
Comprehensive management of both Active (outgoing) and Passive (incoming) invoices. Automates transmission to the SDI (Sistema di Interscambio), handles digital signatures, and monitors invoice states in real-time. 

> **IMPORTANT**: To receive supplier invoices, you need to register our Recipient Code on the Italian Revenue Agency's website. Please follow this [step-by-step guide](https://openapi.it/blog/registrare-codice-destinatario-agenzia-entrate-italiana) and provide the following code when required: **PIC7CPS**

--- 

### 3. Smart Digital Receipts (Legacy Service)
This functional service allows you to issue and transmit electronic receipts for online or physical sales without a traditional telematic recorder. 

- **Configuration**: To use the receipt transmission service, you must enable your credentials on the Italian Revenue Agency (Agenzia delle Entrate) portal by following the third-party assignment procedure. These credentials must be entered into your **IT-configuration** (section `receipts_authentication`).
- **Enablement**: 👉 **[CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE ENABLEMENT PROCEDURE GUIDE](https://docs.openapi.it/Procedura-manuale-per-incarico.pdf)**
- **Transmission Rules**: Please note that you can not send Receipts between **23:55 and 00:00 (Italian Time Zone)**. Receipts sent in this window will be automatically queued and sent in the first minutes of the new day.

*Note: Freelancers (liberi professionisti) and sole proprietorships (aziende individuali) cannot currently appoint a third-party representative for automated receipt transmission.*

> ### ⚠️ Associations & Cooperatives (Associazioni e Cooperative)
> Organizations structured as **associations** (associazioni) or **cooperatives** (cooperative) require a **dedicated configuration** before automated receipt transmission can be activated — the standard onboarding flow does not apply.
>
> **Please [contact our support team](https://openapi.com/contact-us) before starting the integration.** We will guide you through the specific setup required for your organization type.

---

### 4. Advanced E-Receipts & Infrastructure (New Service)
The new E-Receipts (Corrispettivi) service supports points of sale through a structured hierarchy of **Stores (PEM)** and **Cash Registers**. It lives on its own endpoints — `POST /IT-e-receipts`, `GET /IT-e-receipts`, `GET /IT-e-receipts/{id}`, `PATCH /IT-e-receipts/{id}` (return), `DELETE /IT-e-receipts/{id}` (void) — with a dedicated subscription, separate from the Smart Receipts service described above. By default, the system issues sales receipts (`type: sale`).

**Advanced Operations (Extra Features)**:
In addition to standard sales, the system handles special tax scenarios by changing the document `type` to `return` or `void`:
- **Return with Proof (Case A)**: Use the `POSTEReceiptProof` schema to link an operation to a fiscal document (providing `proof` and `document_date`).
- **Different Device Return (Case B)**: Use the `POSTEReceiptDifferentPem` schema for operations on receipts issued by a different PEM (mandatory: `device_id`, `document_number`, `document_date`).

**Key Information**:
- **Provisioning**: Adding new Stores/Registers takes **60-120 seconds**. Components are ready when their status becomes `ONLINE`.
- **Pricing**: each point of sale (Store/PEM) has an **annual fee of € 9.00**, charged from your wallet balance from the first year, none excluded. This fee covers the point of sale and every cash register configured within it — cash registers have no separate cost. It is billed in addition to the per-document price of `POST /IT-e-receipts`. Renewal is attempted automatically about 1 month before `paid_until` expires; if your balance is insufficient, the point of sale keeps working and you receive an early-renewal notice, and only if it is not renewed by the real expiry date is it suspended (`deactivated_reason: unpaid`). A suspended point of sale can be reactivated at any time with `PATCH /IT-store/{id}`, which charges the fee again; `years` (1-10) lets you prepay multiple years at once. See the `Store` schema and the `PATCH /IT-store/{id}` and `DELETE /IT-store/{id}` operations for the full lifecycle.
- **Operational Guide**: Procedures for technical interruptions (Outage) or planned closures (Inactivity) are detailed in our manual:
👉 **[OUTAGE & INACTIVITY MANAGEMENT GUIDE](https://docs.openapi.it/invoice/outage-management-guide.html)**

**NB**: To issue and transmit electronic receipts, you must register a valid **VAT Number** (Partita IVA) as your `fiscal_id`.

fiscal_id.description: French company identifier: a SIREN (9 digits) or a SIRET (14 digits). It identifies the party and is the address used to deliver the invoice on the e-invoicing network. For `sender` it must be a registered configuration of your account (in self-billing, the buyer issuing the document). Same meaning as `siren` / `siret`: send only one of the three.

siren.description: SIREN: 9-digit identifier of the company as a legal entity, assigned by INSEE. Alternative to `siret` / `fiscal_id`.

siret.description: SIRET: 14-digit identifier of one establishment of the company (the 9-digit SIREN followed by a 5-digit establishment number). Preferred when the party invoices from a specific site. Alternative to `siren` / `fiscal_id`.

vat_id.description:
Intra-community VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire): `FR` + 2-character key + the 9-digit SIREN, e.g. `FR32123456789` for SIREN 123456789. Use the number the company actually holds. Unlike SIREN/SIRET it is not used to deliver the invoice: it is a tax identifier written in the legal document. Also accepted as `vat_number`.

- `sender`: optional, the number registered with your configuration is used.
- `recipient`, ordinary invoices and credit notes: the buyer's VAT number, recommended.
- `recipient`, self-billed documents (types 389, 261): the **seller's** VAT number, since in self-billing the recipient is the seller. Required when any line carries VAT (EN 16931 rule BR-S-02), otherwise the request is rejected with error 903. It can be omitted only for sellers not registered for VAT (e.g. franchise en base de TVA), whose lines are all at 0%.

email.description: Email address used as last-resort delivery fallback. If the recipient cannot be reached via Peppol or fr-dgfip, the invoice is delivered to this address as a Factur-X PDF attachment.

external_status.description:
Delivery status reported by the external network. Set to `submitted` on initial send; updated automatically via webhook.

| Value | Macro `state` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `submitted` | — | Invoice submitted to the network |
| `cleared` | SENT | Accepted by the clearance network (France) |
| `succeeded` | SENT | Delivered to recipient's access point |
| `acknowledged` | SENT | Receipt acknowledged by recipient |
| `in_process` | SENT | Being processed by recipient |
| `accepted` | DONE | Accepted by recipient |
| `conditionally_accepted` | DONE | Accepted with conditions |
| `partially_paid` | DONE | Partially paid |
| `paid` | DONE | Fully paid |
| `no_action_taken` | ERROR | No response from recipient |
| `failed` | ERROR | Delivery failed |
| `rejected` | ERROR | Rejected by recipient |
| `under_query` | ERROR | In dispute — clarification requested |
| `received` | — | Inbound document received (passive flow only) |

network.description: Channel through which the invoice was actually delivered, recorded once delivery is confirmed (e.g. `peppol`, `email`). It reflects what happened, not what was requested: an invoice routed to a national network may be delivered by email when that network is unavailable for the recipient. `null` until delivery is confirmed.

service_code.description: Chorus Pro service code for B2G routing.

submission_date.description: Timestamp of submission to the network.

document_number.description: Unique invoice identifier assigned by the sender.

type.description:
UN/CEFACT 1001 document type code, from the French (DGFiP) list. Any other value is rejected with error 918.

**Invoices** (total_amount_including_tax > 0): 380 = Commercial invoice (Facture commerciale), 384 = Corrective invoice (Facture rectificative), 386 = Advance payment invoice (Facture d'acompte), 389 = Self-billed invoice (Facture auto-facturée), 393 = Factored invoice (Facture affacturée), 472 = Factored corrective invoice (Facture rectificative affacturée).

**Credit notes** (total_amount_including_tax < 0): 381 = Credit note (Avoir), 261 = Self-billed credit note (Avoir auto-facturé), 262 = Global discount credit note (Avoir pour remise globale), 396 = Factored credit note (Avoir affacturé), 503 = Advance payment invoice credit note (Avoir de facture d'acompte).

`billing_reference` is required for all credit notes except 262, and for corrective invoices (384, 472).

**Self-billing** (389, 261): the invoice is issued by the buyer on behalf of the seller, under a prior self-billing agreement between them. `sender` is the buyer issuing the document (the registered configuration), `recipient` is the seller receiving it; in the legal document the recipient appears as seller and the sender as buyer. Self-billed documents are delivered only through the e-invoicing network, never by email: if the seller cannot receive self-billed documents, the request is rejected with 422. Self-billing towards public administrations (`chorus_pro_service_code`) is not allowed. When any line carries VAT, `recipient.vat_id` (the seller's VAT number) is required (EN 16931 rule BR-S-02), otherwise the request is rejected with error 903.

total_amount_including_tax.description: Total amount including VAT. Required. Must be > 0 for invoice types, must be < 0 for credit note types (381, 261, 262, 396, 503). Accepts also `amount_including_tax` as alias.

billing_reference.description: Reference to the original invoice being corrected. Required for credit notes (381, 261, 396, 503) and corrective invoices (384, 472); optional for 262; ignored otherwise.

chorus_pro_service_code.description: Specific service code for B2G (Chorus Pro) routing.

attachments.description: Invoice attachments. Required for B2B invoices: the first attachment must be the base64-encoded PDF of the invoice, used by the provider to build the Factur-X (PDF/A-3 with embedded XML) when the recipient is not reachable via Peppol. Not required for B2G (Chorus Pro).

document.description: Base64-encoded file content. For B2B invoices the first attachment must be a PDF (the visual representation of the invoice).

document_id.description: Identifier for the attachment (max 64 characters). Defaults to the invoice document_number.

state.description:
Macro lifecycle state of the invoice.

- `NEW` — Created, not yet submitted to the network
- `SENT` — Submitted and in transit or being processed (external_status: cleared, succeeded, acknowledged, in_process)
- `RECEIVED` — Incoming invoice received from a supplier (passive flow)
- `DONE` — Accepted or paid (external_status: accepted, conditionally_accepted, partially_paid, paid)
- `ERROR` — Delivery or acceptance failed (external_status: failed, rejected, no_action_taken, under_query)

period.description: Reporting period as a date range in the exact format 'YYYY-MM-DD - YYYY-MM-DD' (spaces around the dash are required).

b2c_transactions.description: Aggregated B2C totals for the period (pre-computed by the client). The VAT breakdown is built from vat_amount and vat_rate: when vat_rate is omitted it is derived from the amounts.

date.description: Date the aggregated totals refer to.

category.description: Nature of the transactions being reported (Flux 10 CategoryCode, Annexe 7 G1.68 of the French specification). TLB1 = supplies of goods, TPS1 = supplies of services, TNT1 = operations not subject to French VAT, TMA1 = margin-scheme operations. Mandatory, and it cannot be derived on your behalf: an absent or unknown value makes the tax authority reject the whole filing, so we reject the request instead. Report goods and services as separate entries.

vat_rate.description: VAT rate as a percentage. Optional: derived from the amounts when omitted.

transactions_count.description: Number of transactions aggregated in this entry.

vat_payment_option.description: VAT payment option declared for the entry, when the seller's regime requires it.

b2bi_invoices.description: Cross-border invoices to report. Each entry must identify the invoice it reports: both document_id and issue_date are mandatory. The seller's VAT identifier is added automatically from your configuration and must not be repeated here.

issue_date.description: Issue date of the invoice being reported (not the reporting date).

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code of the invoice.

buyer_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the buyer.

period.description: Reporting period as a date range in the exact format 'YYYY-MM-DD - YYYY-MM-DD' (spaces around the dash are required).

b2bi_payments.description: Payments received on cross-border invoices. Each entry must identify the invoice it refers to: both document_id and issue_date are mandatory, and issue_date is the invoice date, not the payment date.

document_id.description: Number of the invoice the payment refers to.

issue_date.description: Issue date of the invoice the payment refers to.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code of the payment.

vat_rate.description: VAT rate as a percentage. Optional: derived from the amounts when omitted.

type.description:
UN/CEFACT 1001 document type code. Any other value is rejected with error 918.

380 = Commercial invoice (Rechnung, default), 389 = Self-billed invoice (Gutschrift, §14 Abs. 2 UStG), 381 = Credit note, 261 = Self-billed credit note. The sign of total_amount_including_tax must match: positive for 380/389, negative for 381/261. For 381 and 261, billing_reference is required.

**Self-billing** (389, 261): the invoice is issued by the buyer on behalf of the seller, under a prior agreement between them. `sender` is the buyer issuing the document (the registered configuration), `recipient` is the seller receiving it; in the legal document the recipient appears as seller and the sender as buyer. - `NEW` — Created, not yet submitted to the network
- `SENT` — Submitted and in transit or being processed (external_status: cleared, succeeded, acknowledged, in_process)
- `RECEIVED` — Incoming invoice received from a supplier (passive flow)

sdi_status.description:
Technical status assigned by the SDI (Sistema di Interscambio). Possible values:

* **BOOKED**: The invoice is queued and waiting to be processed.
* **SENT**: The invoice has been successfully forwarded to the SDI.
* **DELIVERED**: The invoice has been successfully delivered to the recipient. **Final State**
* **NOT_DELIVERED**: The digital address was unreachable; the invoice is available in the recipient's Tax Portal. **Final State**
* **RECEIVED**: Technical status identifying an incoming (passive) invoice. **Final State**
* **ACCEPTED**: (PA only) The Public Administration has formally accepted the invoice. **Final State**
* **REJECTED**: (PA only) The Public Administration has formally rejected the invoice. **Final State**
* **TERMS_EXPIRED**: (PA only) The 15-day period for PA response has passed. **Final State**
* **ERROR**: The SDI rejected the file due to formal or validation errors. **Final State**

method.description: Specify the callback method. When set to 'POST', a standard HTTP POST request will be initiated with the Content-Type header set to application/x-www-form-urlencoded. If the method is set to 'JSON', a direct HTTP POST request will be made with the Content-Type header set to application/json. The raw JSON data will be directly inserted into the request body without any encoding.

field.description: This parameter works in conjunction with the 'method' parameter set to 'POST'. When provided as a string, it determines the name of the parameter that will be sent in the POST request.

url.description: A valid URL capable of handling POST requests must be entered into this parameter. For endpoints requiring authentication, the 'headers' parameter can be used to specify 'basic auth' or 'bearer auth'. The maximum timeout is 30 seconds. If 'retry' is set, the system will retry up to 'retry' times until a 200 status code is received.

retry.description: The maximum number of attempts is defined by the 'retry' parameter. If the maximum number of attempts is reached without a successful status code (e.g., 200 OK), the request is considered a final failure. A time interval is often introduced between attempts to avoid overloading the server. This interval may increase exponentially with each attempt to reduce the impact on an overloaded server. The 'retry' parameter is configured to retry the request only in case of specific status codes, typically those indicating temporary errors (e.g., 502, 503) or network issues.

headers.description: A collection of HTTP headers to be sent with the request. Each header is defined as a key-value pair. Headers can be used for various purposes, including authentication, content negotiation, and custom metadata.

custom.description: This object can be populated with any additional data you wish to include in the callback response. This data will be accessible within the 'custom' parameter of the callback function. You can use this to store and retrieve any relevant information that you need for your application.

get.description: Returns a list of all French configurations (Legal Entities) associated with your account.

post.description:
This endpoint creates a new configuration and synchronizes data with the external network. It automatically generates the Legal Entity, registration on the Peppol network (via SIREN/SIRET), and VAT setting (FR:VAT). If the VAT number is not provided, it will be automatically calculated from the SIREN.

**This call does NOT register the company on the French national Annuaire (DGFiP/PPF).** Peppol registration and Annuaire registration are separate and independent — being discoverable on Peppol does not mean the company is listed in the Annuaire, and this endpoint never performs that second registration automatically. To register the Annuaire, call `PATCH /FR-configurations/{fiscal_id}/annuaire` afterwards — see that endpoint's description for why it's a separate, explicit step.

**Since September 1, 2026, registering the Annuaire is mandatory to receive invoices** under the French e-invoicing reform — for every company with a French VAT number, regardless of size (only issuing has a size-based deferral, until September 2027 for SMEs/micro-businesses). If `supplier_invoice` is `true` for this configuration, register the Annuaire right after creating it.

409.description: Conflict - The fiscal_id is already registered.

The system validates the new data (e.g., address, send/receive enablement), updates the Legal Entity on the external service in real-time, and saves the changes to the local database.

delete.description:
Allows for the complete removal of a company configuration. 

**What happens on submission:**
1. **External Closure:** The system contacts the external service to delete the Legal Entity and permanently revoke the company's Peppol registration.
2. **Local Removal:** If the deletion on the external provider is successful, the configuration is also permanently deleted from the database.

**Blocked while the Annuaire (DGFiP/PPF) registration is active.** If `annuaire` is set (see `GET /FR-configurations/{fiscal_id}`), this call fails with `422`: deleting the Legal Entity here does not close that separate registration, which would otherwise be left pointing to an account that no longer exists, blocking any future PDP from taking it over. Close it first with `DELETE /FR-configurations/{fiscal_id}/annuaire`.

post.description:
Submits a French electronic invoice (B2B or B2G) to the national clearing network.

**Delivery cascade (B2B)**:
The system attempts delivery in this order, stopping at the first success:
1. **Peppol** — recipient looked up by SIREN/SIRET on the Peppol network.
2. **fr-dgfip** — France's national PPF network (production only; not active in sandbox).
3. **Email** — invoice delivered as a Factur-X PDF attachment to `recipient.email`. Only used if `recipient.email` is provided and no network channel succeeds. Never used for self-billed documents (types 389, 261): they are delivered only through the network, otherwise the request is rejected with 422.

**Document types**: besides commercial invoices (380) and credit notes (381), the French DGFiP types for corrective, advance payment, factored and self-billed documents are supported — see the `type` field.

**B2G routing (Chorus Pro)**: the invoice is treated as B2G — and routed to the centralized Chorus Pro Peppol identifier instead of the recipient's SIREN/SIRET — if **either** of these fields is present and non-empty:
- `chorus_pro_service_code` (root level)
- `details.service_code`

These two are equivalent; setting either one is enough to switch the whole invoice to B2G mode. **B2B `attachments` are NOT required for B2G** — Chorus Pro consumes the UBL/XML directly, no PDF/Factur-X wrapper is generated.

**Testing email delivery in sandbox**: the fr-dgfip network is not active in the test environment. To trigger email delivery, provide `recipient.email` and use a SIREN/SIRET not registered on Peppol — the system will automatically fall back to email.

SelfBilling389.description: Issued by a wholesaler (the buyer, `sender`, registered configuration) on behalf of its supplier (the seller, `recipient`). In the legal document the supplier appears as seller. Delivered only through the e-invoicing network: no email fallback.

B2G.description: `chorus_pro_service_code` switches the invoice to B2G routing. No `attachments` needed — Chorus Pro is fed the XML directly.

post.summary: Send a payment-received notification for a French invoice
post.description:
Sends the "Encaissée" payment-cycle notification for a French invoice that has already been submitted through `POST /FR-invoices`.

This is a legal requirement (not optional) for sellers under the French cash-VAT regime (TVA sur les encaissements), where VAT becomes due at the moment of payment collection rather than at invoice issuance — for these sellers, the official "paid" status must be declared for every invoice once collected. Sellers under the standard VAT regime (due at issuance) do not need to call this endpoint.

This cannot happen automatically: nobody has visibility into the buyer's bank account, so the seller must call this endpoint once payment is received. The VAT breakdown of the notification is derived automatically from the original invoice's tax data — it does not need to be provided again.

patch.summary: Register the French national Annuaire (DGFiP/PPF) for an existing configuration
patch.description:
Registers the `dgfip` network entry (French national Annuaire) for a configuration already onboarded via `POST /FR-configurations`.

**Peppol registration and Annuaire registration are separate.** Creating a configuration only registers the company on Peppol — it does not automatically register it on the national Annuaire, which is required for the `fr-dgfip` delivery network described on `POST /FR-invoices` to actually find the recipient. This granular action is a distinct, opt-in step for that reason: unlike Peppol onboarding, a company migrating from another PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) may still have the addressing line held by that previous provider, and this call would fail until it is released there — keeping it separate from the rest of the configuration means that situation never blocks the Peppol registration, which already works independently, nor a routine `PATCH /FR-configurations/{fiscal_id}` on other fields.

`start_date` must be at least today + 2 calendar days (a Storecove requirement that applies even to a brand-new registration, not only to a provider switch); if omitted, it defaults to that minimum. Calling this action twice for the same `fiscal_id` fails once an Annuaire registration is already active — see the `annuaire` field on `GET /FR-configurations/{fiscal_id}`.

**Switching from another PDP:** the previous provider must close the existing Annuaire entry before this call can succeed; coordinate `start_date` with that closure.

**Mandatory since September 1, 2026 for receiving invoices** under the French e-invoicing reform, for every company with a French VAT number regardless of size (only the issuing obligation has a size-based deferral, until September 2027 for SMEs/micro-businesses). If your configuration has `supplier_invoice: true`, this call should already have been made.

parameters.description: SIREN or SIRET of an existing FR configuration (must already be onboarded on Peppol via POST /FR-configurations).

delete.summary: Close the French national Annuaire (DGFiP/PPF) registration for an existing configuration
delete.description:
Closes the `dgfip` network entry (French national Annuaire) registered via `PATCH /FR-configurations/{fiscal_id}/annuaire`, without touching the rest of the configuration.

**Removes only this identifier.** The Peppol registration (`FR:SIRENE`/`FR:SIRET`, created at onboarding) is a separate identifier and is not affected — only the Annuaire entry is closed.

**When to use it:** when a customer is leaving to use a different PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) for receiving invoices. Closing the Annuaire entry here is what allows the new PDP to register it on their side — without this step, the entry keeps pointing to this account and blocks the switch.

**No propagation-time guarantee:** there is no documented delay before the entry becomes available to a new PDP after this call succeeds — coordinate timing directly with the customer and their new provider.

`DELETE /FR-configurations/{fiscal_id}` (the full configuration) refuses to proceed while an Annuaire registration is still active, specifically to prevent this entry from being orphaned — close it here first.

parameters.description: SIREN or SIRET of an existing FR configuration with an active Annuaire registration.

post.description:
Sends an international B2B invoice from a registered sender country to a foreign recipient.

**Prerequisite — create the country configuration first.** Before sending, you must register a configuration for the sender's country (France: `POST /FR-configurations`, Germany: `POST /DE-configurations`). The sender is matched to that configuration by its fiscal identifier (`sender.fiscal_id`). If no configuration exists for that identifier, the request fails with `404`.

**Recipient rules.** `recipient.country` must be different from `sender.country` — for domestic invoices use the country-specific endpoint instead. `recipient.email` is mandatory and is used for international delivery routing.

**Lifecycle.** The invoice is created in state `NEW` and transitions to `SENT` / `DONE` / `ERROR` automatically as delivery status webhooks are received.

post.description:
Submits a German electronic invoice to the Peppol network.

**B2B (ZUGFeRD)** — recipient identified by `DE:VAT` on Peppol. A PDF attachment is **required**: the EN 16931 XML is embedded inside the PDF to produce a ZUGFeRD-compliant PDF/A-3 document.

**B2G (XRechnung)** — the invoice is treated as B2G if **any** of these fields is present and non-empty:
- `recipient.leitweg_id`
- `leitweg_id` (root level)
- `details.leitweg_id`
- `buyer_reference` (root level, alias of `leitweg_id`)

These four are **equivalent, not cumulative** — setting just one of them is enough to switch the whole invoice to B2G mode. In B2G mode: `attachments` are **not required** (XRechnung is XML-only, no PDF wrapper), and the Leitweg-ID is used as the `DE:LWID` Peppol identifier. **Common mistake**: removing one of these fields to force B2B while another is still set (e.g. clearing `buyer_reference` but leaving `recipient.leitweg_id`) — the invoice stays B2G because any single field is sufficient.

**Delivery cascade (B2B and B2G):**
1. **Peppol** — recipient looked up by DE:VAT (B2B) or DE:LWID (B2G).
2. **Email fallback** — if `recipient.email` is provided and Peppol lookup fails, the invoice is delivered by email. Strongly recommended for B2G since not all German PAs are on Peppol.

**Test Leitweg-ID for B2G sandbox:** `10101010-STO-10`

**VAT rates:** standard 19%, reduced 7% (food, books, passenger transport). Use `tax_category: "exempt"` for zero-rated lines.

post.description:
Send an electronic invoice (XML format) to the SDI.

**Requirements**:
To use this service, you must enable the `customer_invoice` option in your `IT-configuration`.

**Invoice Flow and Notification States**:
After submission, the system sends a **Webhook notification** to your configured endpoint at every status change. The main states you will receive are:
* **NEW**: Invoice created system-side.
* **SENT**: Invoice transmitted to the SDI (intermediary state).
* **RECEIVED**: Used exclusively for the passive invoice flow (inbound invoices).
* **ERROR**: **Final State** indicating a transmission failure or rejection (triggered by `ERROR` or `REJECTED` SDI statuses).
* **DONE**: **Final State** indicating the process was completed successfully (triggered by `DELIVERED`, `ACCEPTED`, `TERMS_EXPIRED`, or `NOT_DELIVERED` SDI statuses).

**SDI Status Details (`details.sdi_status`)**:
The `details.sdi_status` field in the notification payload provides the video technical status from the Revenue Agency:
* **BOOKED**: The invoice is queued and waiting to be processed.
* **SENT**: The invoice has been successfully forwarded to the SDI.
* **DELIVERED**: The invoice has been successfully delivered to the recipient's digital address. **Final State**
* **NOT_DELIVERED**: The invoice is available in the recipient's Tax Portal (*Cassetto Fiscale*) because the digital address was unreachable or missing. **Final State**
* **RECEIVED**: Technical status identifying an incoming (passive) invoice. **Final State**
* **ACCEPTED**: (PA only) The Public Administration has formally accepted the invoice. **Final State**
* **REJECTED**: (PA only) The Public Administration has rejected the invoice. **Final State**
* **TERMS_EXPIRED**: (PA only) The 15-day period for PA acceptance has passed; the invoice is now legally considered accepted. **Final State**
* **ERROR**: The SDI rejected the file due to formal or validation errors. **Final State**

**Special Case: PA Invoices**:
For invoices addressed to the **Public Administration (FPA12)**, the status **DELIVERED** is **not final**. The system will keep the invoice in the **SENT** state until a formal response is received (**ACCEPTED**, **REJECTED**, or **TERMS_EXPIRED**). Only these outcomes will trigger the final **DONE** or **ERROR** state.

**Autofatture (Self-Invoices)**:
The system automatically handles self-invoices (types TD16 through TD28). For these document types, the system extracts the authorizing `fiscal_id` from the `CessionarioCommittente` (Recipient) instead of the `CedentePrestatore` (Sender). You can send these documents to this same endpoint by simply providing the correct `<TipoDocumento>` code in your XML.

**Sandbox Environment & Timing**:
* **Processing Time**: In both test and production, the status transitions from **BOOKED** to **SENT** within 60 seconds.
* **Webhook Notifications**: Webhooks are triggered every 60 seconds. Expect a total delay of approximately 120 seconds from the initial booking to receive the first notification.

**Digital Signature & PA Invoices**:
* **Mandatory Signing**: Invoices addressed to the **Public Administration (FPA12)** MUST be digitally signed.
* **Automatic Signing**: Openapi applies its digital signature automatically if no custom credentials are provided.
* **Custom Signing**: Provide your own certificate credentials in the request headers if you wish to use a custom signature.

**Price esignature**: The invoice is signed via our signing system using EU-QES_automatic. Any applicable costs or subscriptions are automatically deducted if the service is active for your account. You can view the full signature details by clicking [EU-QES_automatic](https://console.openapi.com/it/apis/esignature/documentation#scope=POST:esignature.openapi.com/EU-QES_automatic) 

**Reliability & SDI Availability**:
In the rare event of SDI temporary unavailability, the system will automatically retry the transmission after 5 minutes, then 10, then 15, and so on.

**Note**: The `DatiTrasmissione` block in the uploaded XML will be automatically updated by our system to ensure correct routing.

parameters.description: Your digital signature service username. Required only for custom signing.

parameters.description: Your digital signature service password. Required only for custom signing.

SENT.description:
Status **SENT**: The outgoing invoice has been successfully transmitted to the SDI (Sistema di Interscambio). It is now being processed or has been delivered to the recipient.

- **Direction**: outgoing
- **Technical Context**: Matches `sdi_status` like 'SENT'.

RECEIVED.description:
Status **RECEIVED**: A passive (incoming) invoice from a supplier has been received by the platform and is available for your company.

- **Direction**: incoming
- **Technical Context**: Triggers when a supplier sends an invoice to your Recipient Code (PIC7CPS).

ERROR.description:
Status **ERROR**: The transmission to the SDI failed or the invoice was rejected by the tax authority due to formal errors (Scarto).

- **Direction**: outgoing
- **Technical Context**: Matches `sdi_status` like 'REJECTED' or 'ERROR'. See `sdi_message` for error details.

DONE.description:
Status **DONE**: The transmission process is considered complete. For outgoing invoices, this often corresponds to 'NOT_DELIVERED','RECEIVED', 'ACCEPTED',  'TERMS_EXPIRED'.

- **Direction**: outgoing
- **Technical Context**: Indicates no further statuses are expected for this invoice from SDI.

This service allows you to issue a **Smart Receipt**: the digital receipt service that replaces the telematic cash register for online sales, with transmission handled on your behalf.

**Requirements**: the `receipts` option must be enabled in your `IT-configuration`, together with valid `receipts_authentication` credentials (third-party assignment on the Italian Revenue Agency portal).

**Callback Notifications**: details are updated based on events like `receipt`, `receipt-error`, or `receipt-retry`.

**Transmission Rules**: receipts cannot be transmitted between **23:55 and 00:00 (Italian Time Zone)**. Receipts submitted in that window are queued with status `waiting` and sent in the first minutes of the new day.

**This endpoint only issues sales.** It has no `type` field: to return items from a receipt use `PATCH /IT-receipts/{id}`, to void it use `DELETE /IT-receipts/{id}`. Both create a new linked receipt carrying `parent_receipt_id`. Sending `type` (or any other unknown key) is rejected with error 341.

> **Looking for stores and cash registers?** The **E-Receipts (Corrispettivi)** service — stores, cash registers, returns with proof of purchase, returns from a different device — lives on its own endpoint with a dedicated subscription: see `POST /IT-e-receipts`.

post.description:
This service issues an **E-Receipt (Corrispettivo)** for points of sale: the document is transmitted through the Store (PEM) and Cash Register registered in your `IT-configuration`.

**Requirements**: the `e_receipts` option must be enabled in your `IT-configuration`, the `fiscal_id` must be a valid 11-digit VAT number, and at least one Store with a completed onboarding (`pem_serial` present) must exist.

**Infrastructure & Ownership**:
You can provide `cashier_id`, `store_id`, and `cr_id`.
- If a `cashier_id` is provided, the system validates its existence and ownership and issues the document on behalf of that cashier.
- If `cr_id` is provided, the system strictly uses that register (ownership check applies).
- If `store_id` is provided without `cr_id`, the system uses the first available register in that store.
- If no IDs are provided, the system falls back to the default store/register.
**NB**: Providing an ID that does not belong to your configuration will result in a **403 Forbidden** error.

**Special Operations**:
By default the system issues sales receipts (`type: sale`). Advanced tax scenarios are handled by changing the document `type` to `return` or `void`:
- **With Proof of Purchase**: to link a return or void to an existing fiscal proof, use the `POSTEReceiptProof` schema (providing `proof` and `document_date`).
- **Different Device (PEM)**: to operate on receipts issued by another device, use the `POSTEReceiptDifferentPem` schema (mandatory: `device_id`, `document_number`, `document_date`).
- **Standard return or void** of a document issued by this service does not go through this endpoint: use `PATCH /IT-e-receipts/{id}` (return) or `DELETE /IT-e-receipts/{id}` (void).

**Payments must balance the items total**:
The sum of the payment fields must equal the total of the `items` (quantity × unit_price, net of item discounts), otherwise the document is rejected. Payment fields: `cash_payment_amount`, `electronic_payment_amount`, `ticket_restaurant_payment_amount` (with `ticket_restaurant_quantity`), `services_uncollected_amount`, `goods_uncollected_amount`, `discount` (discount to pay), `rounding_up` / `rounding_down` (mandatory cash rounding under DL 50/2017, allowed only when cash is the sole payment method, always positive; `rounding_up` is subtracted from the collected total).

> **NB**: This service is billed on its own subscription, separate from `POST /IT-receipts` (Smart Receipts).

e_receipt_proof.description: Return of goods sold by a document that is not available in the system: the customer proof is declared through `proof` (POS, VR or ND) and `document_date`.

e_receipt_different_pem.description: Return of a document issued by another device: `device_id`, `document_number` and `document_date` are all mandatory.

Dismisses a point of sale: the fiscal device is decommissioned, the annual fee stops renewing and no new document can be issued from its cash registers. The residual, already-paid portion of the current year's fee is **not refunded**.

**The operation is not reversible.** The device serial cannot be reused: to resume business at that location, add a new point of sale to the configuration. Existing documents remain available, and the point of sale keeps appearing in the configuration with `active: false`, `status: DISCARDED` and `deactivated_reason: deleted` — records are never removed.

If the fiscal device cannot be decommissioned, the request fails and nothing is changed on your configuration: this prevents a point of sale from remaining registered with the Italian Revenue Agency while no longer being served.

To suspend a point of sale temporarily (holidays, closures) do not use this endpoint: see the `inactivity-communication` action on `POST /IT-store/{id}/{action}`.

patch.summary: Reactivate a point of sale, or prepay future years.
patch.description:
Reactivates a point of sale suspended because the annual fee was not renewed (`deactivated_reason: unpaid`), or prepays future years on an already active one.

**Fee**: € 9.00 per year, per point of sale (all cash registers within it are included at no extra cost). Charged from your wallet balance, not from a subscription.

Only `active: true` is accepted: a point of sale cannot be deactivated from here — use `DELETE /IT-store/{store_id}`.

The optional `years` field (1-10) prepays multiple years at once: the new expiry always extends from the current one if it has not passed yet, or from today if it has, charging € 9.00 × `years`. Without `years`, the historical behavior applies: free if the fee is still valid, charged € 9.00 for one year if expired — unless a renewal notice is pending (`renewal_notice_sent_at` set), in which case the charge is applied anyway even though the fee has not expired yet, so the customer can complete the early renewal requested by the notice. Insufficient credit leaves the point of sale unchanged.

A point of sale with `deactivated_reason: deleted` cannot be reactivated: its fiscal device has been decommissioned, so a new point of sale must be created.

years.description: Optional number of years to prepay at once. Defaults to 1 year of coverage when omitted.
